text:
alex: Heads up — we're seeing ~30 requests in the last hour that claim x-api-version: 2 but were routed to the v1 pool. Repro attached.
maya: Ugh. Any pattern on client id / region? :thinking_face:
alex: Mostly eu-west, client ids look like `client-*-trial`. One curious thing: they include both `x-api-version: 2` and a query param `?version=1` in some cases.
ben: Are we evaluating query param before header in the routing decision? I thought header had precedence.
priya: Telemetry shows our routing classifier returns "ambiguous" for those requests which triggers the quarantine fallback to v1. We log event `routing.version_ambiguity` for those.
alex: Example request (redacted):
```
GET /generate?version=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.com
x-api-version: 2
x-client-id: client-123
User-Agent: SomeSdk/1.2.3
```
maya: Ok that's clearly conflicting. Do we have a documented precedence rule? I couldn't find it in the public API docs.
ben: We do in the internal routing config: `precedence: [header, path, config]` but looks like an older deploy changed the evaluation order in the routing service. Deploy-bot shows a rollout earlier this week.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-02-14T09:12 by infra: routing-service v1.18.3 -> v1.19.0
priya: That v1.19.0 change reordered matchers to optimize latency, but it didn't include the compatibility matrix update. Ops confirmed a missing unit test that would have caught version precedence flips.
alex: Impact: a) some customers unexpectedly hit older model variants (cost + lower quality). b) quota/usage attribution goes to v1 meters; dashboards show weird spikes.
maya: For dashboards: can we tag those requests with `routing.debug_reason=ambiguous` so product can filter? Also add a derived metric `ambiguous_routed_count`.
ben: Quick mitigation: revert the matcher order in routing-service or add a feature-flag that forces header precedence. Which is safer?
priya: Revert + hotfix seems safest. Feature-flag takes longer and we want immediate customer relief.
alex: Agreed. Also need a communication plan: a short console banner + email to tenants with any customer-facing impact.
maya: UX copy draft for console banner: "We detected a small set of requests routed to legacy paths due to conflicting version signals. We're rolling a fix now — no action needed. Reach us at support@redwood.com if you see quality regressions." Thoughts?
ben: Fine. Add an opt-out link for companies on dedicated/private who want immediate control.
priya: Telemetry follow-ups: emit `routing.version_precedence_change` event when routing config changes, and surface a noisy alert if `routing.version_ambiguity` rate > 0.1% of traffic in 5m.
alex: Tests: add an integration test that sends conflicting signals (header vs query vs cookie) and asserts header wins. Also add e2e quota attribution test to ensure token counts map to versioned meters.
maya: I'll own the console banner + email copy. Ben can handle the revert PR and test, Priya will add telemetry and alerts.
ben: I'll open the PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-service/pull/428
priya: I've created a dashboard tile request in observability: "Ambiguous routing" and wired a pager rule draft.
alex: Thanks. Once PR is merged let's run a small canary for 10k reqs and check `ambiguous_routed_count` drop to ~0 before rollout.
maya: Can we also add a developer warning in SDKs when both query param and header are present? Might prevent future trouble.
ben: Good idea. I'll drop a note in devex channel and add a small patch to the JS and Python SDKs.
alex: Great. Coming back with updates in ~30m after the PR lands.
priya: One more note — ensure quota reconciliation job can reassign misattributed tokens for the last 24h window for affected customers. I'll coordinate with billing.
maya: :thumbsup:
alex: PTL. Thanks everyone.
